reference.source: Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation
clinicalPearls: An imprinting disorder causing severe pre- and postnatal growth restriction with relative macrocephaly (head sparing) at birth
Characteristic features include a triangular face, broad forehead, body asymmetry (hemihypotrophy), and fifth-finger clinodactyly
Feeding difficulties, marked failure to thrive, and fasting hypoglycaemia due to low muscle and fat mass are common in infancy
Most cases are explained by loss of methylation at the IC1 (H19/IGF2) region on chromosome 11p15 or by maternal uniparental disomy of chromosome 7
It is broadly the molecular mirror image of Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome, with reduced rather than increased IGF2-driven growth
The Netchine-Harbison clinical scoring system guides diagnosis and directs molecular testing when features are suggestive
Management centres on optimising nutrition and growth, monitoring for hypoglycaemia, and endocrine input including growth-promoting therapy where indicated
reference.pathophysiology: Silver-Russell syndrome is an imprinting disorder most often caused by hypomethylation of the paternally derived IC1 domain at chromosome 11p15, which reduces expression of the growth-promoting gene IGF2, or by maternal uniparental disomy of chromosome 7. Reduced IGF2-driven growth signalling produces profound intrauterine and postnatal growth restriction with relative sparing of head growth. Because the affected loci are imprinted, the parental origin of the epigenetic or chromosomal change determines the phenotype, and body asymmetry reflects mosaic distribution of the molecular defect.
additionalDifferentials: Temple syndrome and other imprinting disorders
3-M syndrome and other primordial short-stature syndromes
additionalInvestigations: Methylation analysis of the 11p15 IC1 region and testing for maternal uniparental disomy of chromosome 7
Chromosomal microarray to exclude copy-number causes of growth restriction
Blood glucose monitoring for fasting hypoglycaemia in infancy
Growth monitoring with assessment of body asymmetry and limb-length discrepancy
Endocrine evaluation including growth hormone axis assessment
Nutritional and feeding assessment for failure to thrive
redFlags: Fasting hypoglycaemia risking neurological harm, especially during intercurrent illness
Severe failure to thrive requiring intensive nutritional support
Significant limb-length discrepancy affecting gait and posture
Signs of relative intracranial disproportion or raised pressure requiring assessment
reference.prognosis: With early nutritional optimisation, hypoglycaemia prevention, and endocrine management, growth and general health improve, though final stature is often below average. Cognition is usually normal or near normal, and adult outcomes are generally favourable with appropriate support.
pitfalls: Attributing severe growth restriction to placental insufficiency alone and not testing for imprinting defects
Missing fasting hypoglycaemia because of the child's small size and low reserves
Overlooking body asymmetry, which is a useful diagnostic clue
Failing to recognise the mirror-image relationship with Beckwith-Wiedemann when interpreting 11p15 results
references: Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation
International consensus statement on the diagnosis and management of Silver-Russell syndrome
management: Nutritional rehabilitation with feeding support and enteral feeding where needed to address failure to thrive, avoiding rapid catch-up adiposity
Prevention and treatment of fasting hypoglycaemia through regular feeds, uncooked cornstarch and an emergency regimen during illness, given the low muscle and fat mass
Recombinant growth hormone therapy to improve growth velocity, body composition and final stature

Orthopaedic management of body asymmetry and limb-length discrepancy with shoe raise or surgery, plus monitoring for and treatment of early or precocious puberty with a gonadotropin-releasing hormone analogue
Coordinated care through clinical genetics, paediatric endocrinology, dietetics, gastroenterology and orthopaedics
Genetic counselling with molecular confirmation of 11p15 hypomethylation or maternal uniparental disomy of chromosome 7, and discussion of recurrence risk
